text.p: Spanish debt market awoke on Monday morning little changed, but dealers expected prices to stay on the downside with negative mood as EMU jitters continue.
"The mood's different now. We are seeing selling pressure every time prices go up," a dealer in Madrid said.
Despite possible good news from February CPI later this week, he said the market "would not react. It already knew, and had already priced in all good macroeconomic news,".
February CPI, due March 13, should show a 0.2 percent monthly increase with the yearly rate declining to 2.8 percent from 2.9 percent in January, according to a Reuter poll.
